title: Pair density Shannon information measures and their $N$-dependent behaviour in diatomic molecular systems
authors: Saul J. C. Salazar, J. Antonio Zarate, J. M. Solano-Altamirano, Humberto G. Laguna, Julio M. Hernandez-Perez, Robin P. Sagar
abstract: Pair density Shannon entropies and mutual information in position and in momentum space are calculated for two series of homonuclear and heteronuclear diatomic molecules using Hartree-Fock wave functions. The pair density entropy sum increases with the quality of the basis set. Mutual information, a measure of statistical correlation, is seen to be smaller in momentum space as compared to position space. The interpretation is that the momentum pair density is closer than the position pair density to a Hartree-like reference. The $N$-dependent behaviours of the entropy and mutual information sums are examined by fitting the data to three different model behaviours. Results show that these models are capable of representing the molecular data in differing degrees. The parameters obtained from a particular model are relatively constant across different chemical series. This adds evidence to the argument of a universal $N$-dependent behaviour of the entropy sums.
summary: This paper applies information theory, specifically Shannon entropy and mutual information, to analyze the pair density properties of diatomic molecules using Hartree-Fock theory. The authors examine how these measures change with system size ($N$) and find evidence for universal scaling laws. This work provides a quantitative, information-theoretic characterization of molecular bonding and correlation.
main_problem: The study investigates pair density Shannon information measures and their dependence on system size ($N$) in diatomic molecules.
main_result: The analysis suggests a potential universal $N$-dependent behavior for the entropy sums, and it finds that momentum space pair density is closer to the Hartree-like reference than position space.
method: Calculations utilize Hartree-Fock wave functions to compute pair density Shannon entropies and mutual information in both position and momentum space.
model_or_system: The physical systems studied are homonuclear and heteronuclear diatomic molecules. The calculations are performed using the Hartree-Fock approximation.
key_observables: Pair density Shannon entropies ($S_\Gamma, S_\Pi, S_T$) and mutual information ($I_r, I_p$).
important_parameters: System size ($N$), basis set quality, and the comparison between position and momentum space representations.
main_assumptions: The analysis is based on Hartree-Fock wave functions, and the study focuses on entropy sums derived from entropic uncertainty relations.
figures_summary: Figures show Shannon entropy sums ($S_t, S_T, I_T$) for neutral and heteronuclear diatomic molecules as a function of $N$, comparing theoretical models to basis set data.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework using Shannon entropy definitions for reduced and pair densities, calculates these measures for diatomic systems in both position and momentum space, and finally examines the $N$-dependent behavior by fitting the data to various theoretical models.
why_interesting: The use of information-theoretic measures like entropy and mutual information to characterize molecular structure and correlation provides a novel, quantitative lens through which to view electronic structure, which is highly relevant to understanding quantum correlations in molecular physics.
